issues: The subject was a grey placeholder dashboard with a tiny alert bar: the pain was unreadable and the tilt looked like a framing mistake
A flat background gave the -10° tilt no reference, so the levelling beat felt weak
After levelling only a small toast changed; the rest of the frame stayed the same and the fix had no weight
changes: Porcelain look (cool white and cobalt) with red used only as a status colour; the subject is a 1320×700 incident panel designed for the shot: 168px p99 latency, a live chart and three status tiles
The world is graph paper larger than the frame: at -10° the grid visibly fights the frame edges, after levelling it locks square, so 'set right' is literal
Levelling beat: 6f wind-up 0.6° further, 13f snappy overshoot to +1.2°, 11f smooth settle to 0, with scale 1.08→1.00

Follow-through: 4f later the number falls 2,840→184 ms and shifts red to ink, the chart heals in a left-to-right wave (stroke turns cobalt point by point) leaving a faint red ghost, the status chip pops to Operational on the frame latency drops under SLO, and the headline becomes 'Rolled back in one click.'
A warm-red screen-space vignette during the tilt clears as it levels; a 1.5% slow push holds the last 60f
